title: CppCon 2017: Fedor Pikus “C++ atomics, from basic to advanced.  What do they really do?”
summary: Fedor Pikus's CppCon 2017 talk on C++ atomics, looking at what they let the programmer express and what the hardware actually does. It covers memory ordering and lock-free programming from basic to advanced.
why: HN recommends it as an enlightening explanation of atomics, caches and memory ordering from a strong presenter.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: Watching this was enlightening to say the least (and the presenter is very good)
